summary: Verified iteration-5 features: (1) assets served from origin as /assets/bitverse-logo.png and /assets/adesh-yash.png (both HTTP 200, image/png), (2) all tags on Home & About use relative /assets/ paths with complete=true/naturalWidth>0, (3) developer photo renders on About page (data-testid=developer-photo, natural=1260), (4) new /api/analytics/trending endpoint returns 20 total_subjects with 8 items, sorted desc, all scores>0 when subject_stats is empty, (5) TrendingChart component renders 9 bars, total activity counter, top-4 cards on desktop AND mobile (no horizontal overflow), (6) live refresh (setInterval 8s) verified — trending endpoint hit 5 times in ~12s, (7) view/download endpoints still return file bytes and $inc counters. All 10 backend pytest tests pass. HOWEVER a critical logic bug in the fallback discovered — see rca.

critical.issue: Fallback deterministic seed applies ONLY when ALL subjects have score==0 (uses `all(r['score']==0 for r in rows)`). As soon as even ONE real view/download is recorded on any subject, the fallback is disabled for EVERY subject, so 19 of 20 subjects show views=0/downloads=0/score=0 and the home-page chart becomes a single-bar chart. Reproducible: I hit /api/files/{id}/view twice on a Physics file — trending chart now shows only Physics bar with height 3, other 7 bars empty. This directly violates the requirement 'chart always looks populated / scores are ALWAYS non-zero'.

issues: Non-blocking recharts warning in console: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' — appears twice during ResponsiveContainer mount before size is measured; does not affect rendering, but noisy in DevTools.

action_items: HIGH: Fix fallback logic in server.py::analytics_trending. Recommended: apply deterministic seed PER-ROW when that row's score==0, not just when ALL rows are zero. Suggested patch: replace the `if all(r['score']==0 ...)` block with `for r in rows: if r['score'] == 0: <compute hash-based views/downloads>`. This keeps real activity intact while filling empty subjects with demo values so the chart always looks alive.
OPTIONAL: Set an explicit minHeight on the ResponsiveContainer wrapper (e.g. min-height: 360px on the parent div) to eliminate the harmless recharts width/height=-1 warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L402 `if all(r['score']==0 for r in rows)` — brittle: single real view kills the demo seed for the other 19 subjects (see critical bug above).

server.py L338-347 & L360-368: try/except that silently swallows *all* exceptions during view_count/subject_stats $inc — masks any Mongo errors. Consider logging the exception (logger.exception) rather than pass.
TrendingChart.jsx L64: `data.map((d) => ({ ...d, shortName: shortName(d.name) }))` recomputes on every render — fine given small array (8), but `useMemo` would silence downstream re-render churn.

TrendingChart.jsx L47-62: setInterval fires setTick which forces the entire BarChart to remount (via `key={tick}`) every 8s — this re-runs the 900ms animation each refresh, which is intentional but slightly heavy. Acceptable.

Assets are served from /app/frontend/public/assets — good; but adesh-yash.png is 1.8MB PNG. Recommend converting to WebP or resizing to ~600px for faster load (esp. on About page where two copies render).
seed_data_creation: None. Trending endpoint's own hash-based seed populates 20 subjects when subject_stats collection is empty.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified: assets/*.png return 200; TrendingChart mounts with 8 bars + top-4 cards; live-refresh setInterval works (5 hits in ~12s); developer-photo renders on About. OUTSTANDING: the trending fallback logic breaks after any real /view or /download call. To reproduce: 1) call /api/files/{id}/view twice on any file with a subject_id — 2) call /api/analytics/trending?limit=8 — 3) observe 19/20 subjects have score=0. After main agent fixes the per-row fallback, re-verify by (a) calling /view a few times, (b) confirming the chart still shows 8 populated bars.
rca_of_the_issue: Bug: single-bar chart after real activity. Location: /app/backend/server.py analytics_trending() around L402. Cause: `if all(r['score'] == 0 for r in rows)` — the moment one subject has a real stat, the deterministic hash seed is skipped for every OTHER subject too. Reproduction: (1) POST or GET /api/files/{file_id}/view where file has subject_id. (2) GET /api/analytics/trending — 19 subjects will now show 0/0/0. Mitigation: change the block to per-row: `for r in rows: if r['score'] == 0: h = int(hashlib.md5(r['name'].encode()).hexdigest(),16); r['views']=(h%240)+60; r['downloads']=(h%90)+20; r['score']=r['views']+r['downloads']*2`. This preserves real activity where present and demo-fills the rest.
